reply:
**Document judged:** the opening of *The Time Machine* (Chapters I–VI, up to the arrival among the Eloi). It answers several questions — whether abstractions are real, what memory is, how the year 802,701 lives. Title and opening make the central one the Time Traveller's case that Time is a fourth dimension of Space and that a machine can carry a body along it. I froze that one.

## 1. The question, frozen

Does a body extend along Time as it extends along Length, Breadth and Thickness, and can a machine move a body along that direction — forward, backward, faster or slower? Range: any real body, at any date. Kind: partly *what produces it*, partly *why can it not happen*. Several jobs arrive from his listeners, not from him; I mark which.

## 2. The parts, in his words

**P1** A line of nil thickness, a plane, an instantaneous cube have no real existence; only bodies with extension are real.
**P2** Any real body must have extension in four directions: Length, Breadth, Thickness and Duration.
**P3** There is no difference between Time and the three dimensions of Space, *except that our consciousness moves along it*.
**P4** We cannot get away from the present moment; we pass along Time with a uniform velocity from the cradle to the grave.
**P5** Vivid recollection is going back to the instant of its occurrence.
**P6** Gravitation limits up-and-down; balloons lifted that limit; a limit on Time may likewise be lifted.
**P7** Two levers — one into the future, one reversing the motion — and a saddle.
**P8** The barometer's traced line runs along the Time-dimension.
**P9** Portraits at eight, fifteen, seventeen are sections of a four-dimensioned being, "fixed and unalterable".
**P10** The Psychologist's "diluted presentation below the threshold" explains our not seeing it.

## 3. Change list

Covered: which lever; the driver's chosen direction; speed relative to us; model or man; whether an observer is watching. Left out, and not said up front: how a lever reaches the time dimension at all; whether the machine keeps its place in Space (the Psychologist raises this, and the owner has the objector answer it); whether a stopped machine collides — a long paragraph, but about stopping, not direction.

## 4. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | **Borrowed** | Rests on an untested view of what "real existence" means; that view is tested nowhere here. |
| P2 | **Held if** | As an *axis*, held by the portrait series and the weather record. As a *direction of travel*, its only job is the one it was invented for. |
| P3 | **Held** | By the Medical Man's "why has it always been regarded as different?" The "except" clause is what pays for it. |
| P4 | **Held** (the no-choice, no-stopping half); **Loose** ("uniform" — any rate would do; he later says he does not know which way the model went) | |
| P5 | **Loose** | Swap "recalling" for "dreaming" and the argument works as well. Near idle: remove it and P6 still answers "why can't we move in Time". |
| P6 | **Held** | By the job "why can't we move in Time, if Time is a dimension?" Swap balloons for aeroplanes and the job is still done, so the held part is more general: *a limit once taken for a law, lifted by a machine*. |
| P7 | **Loose** | No route from lever to displacement is given; a dial would be said to work the same. |
| the reversing lever | **Unknown** | Nothing run bears on it; it is the one change that would separate travel from a trick. |
| P8 | **Held** | The trace genuinely lies in none of the three recognised dimensions. |
| P9 | **Held** | "Fixed and unalterable" does real work for the portrait series. |
| P10 | **Loose** | And a catch-all: covers visible and invisible, past and future, any speed. No gauge offered, and it was supplied by a listener. |

## 5. Whole-explanation checks

**Fixed, and said so.** The story's truth is put outside the test: "I can't argue tonight"; "Most of it will sound like lying. So be it!"

**Flip.** Had the model stayed on the table, nothing would have had to change — he had not wound it, or it went and came back. The claim covers the outcome and its opposite.

**Where the answer sits.** The conclusion — a body can be carried along Time — is placed in the starting points as P2, under the name "extension in Duration". His own tell: "It is only another way of looking at Time."

**Direction.** P8 runs the right way: change the time and the trace moves; draw a longer trace and the day does not move. P5 runs backwards, from remembering to "going back".

**Jobs and their provenance.** Given by the owner: the fourth dimension, the machine. Given by listeners, and this is where the weight sits — "why can't we move in Time?", "you cannot move about in Time", "it would have been visible last Thursday". Added by the guests, doing no work: Hastings, Homer, the investment.

**Pull.** P9 says a four-dimensioned being is fixed and unalterable; P2 says a machine can put you in a different part of it. Also, the more exactly Time is like the other three, the harder the job "why is it always regarded as different?" The joint is the "except" clause. What would show the line is in the wrong place is a case needing the asymmetry but not consciousness.

**Catch-alls and gauges.** "Consciousness" — declared immaterial and without dimensions, so no reading can be taken. "Diluted presentation" — covers every visibility. "I don't, for certain, know which" — covers both directions. None has a gauge.

**Rivals.** Sleight-of-hand: the Tübingen conjuror, last Christmas's ghost, Filby's "against reason", the Psychologist's "humbug". Nothing on the change list tells the two apart; the one lever that could was never tried. At this level they are the same account.

**Where the parts came from.** P6 is *built* (a real case in view). Nearly everything else is *asserted*, P10 by a listener who wants the paradox to work. There is one demonstration and no run of cases, so nothing is *fitted*.

## 6. What would make it harder to vary

1. **Press the other lever.** Send a second model back to a named date — the narrator's own test. It should have been here last Thursday, and should not be. Both halves can be looked at.
2. **Give the catch-alls a gauge.** The document supplies the raw material: "fifty times or a hundred times faster". Fix the reading that would worry him — the model passing a spinning wheel at a stated speed and a stated fraction of its brightness.

## 7. What this does not show

Not that time travel is impossible. Only that the parts are mostly asserted, and the single test does not separate the claim from a trick.

## 8. One next step

Press the reversing lever, against a fixed date.
